subject.title: fix(shared): re-throw non-ENOENT errors in ignore-rules file reading

question: Should an unreadable ignore file abort the owning discovery operation, or should OpenClaw report a diagnostic and continue without that file's rules?
rationale: The PR deliberately converts previously best-effort behavior into fail-closed exception propagation, and source inspection alone cannot determine the intended user-facing failure policy at all callers.

options.title: Confirm fail-closed behavior
options.body: Rethrow every non-ENOENT value and add focused tests and real proof showing the affected discovery caller fails with a useful error.

options.title: Return a diagnostic
options.body: Surface unreadable ignore files through the owning diagnostic channel while continuing discovery under an explicitly documented policy.

options.title: Keep best-effort loading
options.body: Close or narrow the PR if maintainers do not want existing discovery workflows to fail because an optional ignore file is unreadable.

recommendation.title: Confirm fail-closed behavior
recommendation.body: Rethrow every non-ENOENT value and add focused tests and real proof showing the affected discovery caller fails with a useful error.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a core behavior and compatibility choice around the shared skills/discovery surface, where this person has recent adjacent history.
